To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HN protein of PIV3 contains a neuraminidase domain which is structurally conserved between PIV3 and other paramyxoviruses, and a hemagglutinating domain which is structually unique to PIV3.
the HN gene of PIV3 contains a single point mutation which codes for a single amino substitution in the H N protein and that the HN epitopes are located in predicted coil structures.
The hemagglutin neuraminidase gene of human parainflu enza virus 3 (PI V3) was sequenced for 16 antigeni c variants of the virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a molecular model of the HN glycoprotein of PIV3.
the development of a vaccine against parainfluenzavirus type 3 (HPIV3).
the antigenic, structural, and functional properties of the HN glycoprotein of the human PIV3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HN of the human PIV3 is an important antigenic determinant of the virus, that its structure is highly conserved, and that the HN protein is a major determinant in viral attachment to host cell receptors.
the antigenic structure of the PIV3 H N protein is complex and that the HN epitopes are confor mational in nature.
the HN protein is a complex, multivalent glycoprotein which contains several antigenically and structurally distinct regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified several antigenic sites on the HN protein, which are involved in hemagglutinating, neuraminidase and infecting activities, that are located in a predicted coil region of the molecule.
the PIV3 H N protein is a highly glycosylated protein with 10 potential N-linked oligosaccharide chains and that it has a complex secondary structure.

(1) The HN protein of PIV3 is a highly antigenic molecule with at least nine distinct antigenic regions; (2) The HN molecule is composed primarily of hydrophilic beta sheets and random coil structures, and the antigenic regions are located in the coil regions of the molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HN protein is a complex molecule with many different functional domains and that these functional domains are not necessarily contiguous in the linear sequence of the HN gene.

the HN proteins of human and bovine parainfluenzavirus type 3 are highly similar in primary structure but have significant differences in the antigenic determinants recognized by neutralizing monoclonal antibodies.
there are many ways to make a virus resistant to a given antibody, and that it is not necessarily true that a virus will become resistant by changing the epitope that the antibody binds.
